svg.title: What OpenShell and FinGuard achieved together
svg.desc: OpenShell enforced runtime boundaries, FinGuard constrained the investigation workflow, and their integration completed a real-data investigation with independent containment evidence. Results cover a local demonstration, not certification or a comparative safety benchmark.

g.text: FINGUARD / OBSERVED OUTCOMES
One investigation. Two layers of control.
Separate responsibilities, connected by a verifiable execution record.
EXTERNAL RUNTIME BOUNDARY
NVIDIA OpenShell
Controls what the process can access.
• Read-only evidence; restricted file access
• Network destination, method and path rules
• Restricted identity and process controls
• Native supervisor audit evidence
9 / 9 direct I/O probes matched expectations
3 native network denials corroborated blocking
Probes bypassed the FinGuard Guard and Runner.
APPLICATION WORKFLOW CONTROLS
FinGuard Safety Controls
Controls which proposed actions execute.
• Validate tool names and arguments
• Restrict tools to the assigned transaction
• Require evidence before case submission
• Keep labels out; bound the agent loop
2 model calls · 4 tool calls · complete
Required evidence gathered; simulated note recorded.
Completion does not certify reasoning quality.
ACHIEVED TOGETHER
A real-data investigation completed within tested boundaries.
Application evidence + independent runtime observations + native audit
14 / 14 integration checks passed
Local software deployment · banking actions simulated
Takeaway: make useful agent work observable and constrain its execution.
No certification, general prompt-injection guarantee, or measured safety uplift versus a baseline.
The 14 checks combine evidence above; they are not 14 additional independent attack tests.
Source: saved FinGuard reports · verified 2026-10-03T14:02:33.571865+00:00 · OpenShell 0.1.2
